subject: Seasonal usage floor + top-up playbook — NovaWorks renewal window
messages:
From: Ava Thompson <ava@novaworks.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Reed <marcus.reed@novaworks.ai>, procurement@novaworks.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: Seasonal usage floor + top-up options

Hi Ben —

Quick context: we run a pretty pronounced seasonality window (Nov–Jan) and based on last year we expect a 2.5x spike. We’re in the final 90 days of our renewal and want to avoid an overage shock while keeping flexibility. Procurement asked whether Redwood can offer a seasonal floor + short-term top-up arrangement (one-off topup credits for seasonal months) or a temporary uplift that is pro-rated and then reconciled at renewal.

Key constraints:
- Budget bucket must be approved by Oct 12 (binding)
- Procurement needs an SOW or amendment to attach to the PO
- We prefer a predictable per-month commitment for the window rather than daily variable invoice spikes

Can you outline 2–3 executable scenarios (blended uplift, stepped seasonal floor, and committed top-up credits) with approximate unit economics? Marcus and I can share usage patterns if helpful.

Thanks,
Ava
Ava Thompson
Head of Product, NovaWorks
ava@novaworks.ai

-----

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Thompson <ava@novaworks.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@novaworks.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Seasonal usage floor + top-up options

Ava —

Thanks for the clear context. I put together three pragmatic paths that align with how other seasonal customers have executed:

1) Seasonal floor + consumption top-up (recommended)
   - Commit to a seasonal floor (for Nov–Jan) equal to 1.6x your current monthly baseline.
   - Redwood reserves capacity for that window; usage above the floor billed at standard pay-as-you-go.
   - Outcome: predictable committed spend for the window, lower risk of overload; we can offer a 7% uplift discount on the floor vs standard hosted rate.

2) Temporary uplift (pro-rated monthly) + true-up at renewal
   - Increase committed units for Nov–Jan only (pro-rated monthly pricing).
   - At renewal we true-up against actuals and convert unused units to credit or roll forward.
   - Outcome: simpler billing mechanics for procurement but requires negotiation on conversion/credit terms.

3) One-off top-up credits
   - Buy a block of top-up credits for the season (non-expiring within 6 months).
   - Bundle discount applies if block > $50k.
   - Outcome: fastest procurement (single PO) but less operational insulation if actuals exceed block.

I attached a spreadsheet with example math for each scenario (NovaWorks_Uplift_Scenario_v2.xlsx). Lauren, can you drop the exact invoice mechanics and DocuSign path? Marissa — FYI on activation / CS runbook we’d need to stage.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll draft an amendment (SLA_Amendment_Draft.pdf) we can attach to the PO
- We’ll tailor the pricing band to NovaWorks’ Nov–Jan forecast if you share a simple usage CSV
- If procurement needs standard language, we can include a 30-day termination carveout for the uplift window

If the Oct 12 deadline is firm we can aim to lock scenario 1 or 3 this week and route the DocuSign for PO attachment.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Seasonal usage floor + top-up options

Hi all —

Looping in with concrete pricing mechanics and DocuSign checklist. Per Ben’s scenarios, here’s how we typically operationalize each: 

Scenario 1 (seasonal floor + top-up) — operational details:
- Billing: monthly invoice for committed floor amount; overages billed monthly at standard pay-as-you-go rates.
- Discounting: 7% applied to the seasonal floor for the one-off window. If you convert that seasonal floor into a longer-term committed bucket at renewal, we tier discount to 10% for a 12-month conversion (applies only to units converted at renewal).
- Procurement docs: SLA amendment + simple one-page MOU outlining forecast and activation dates.

Scenario 2 (temporary uplift + true-up) — operational details:
- Billing: pro-rated increase invoiced monthly for the uplift months.
- True-up: unused units convert to credits valid for 4 quarters (no cash refunds).
- Conversion to committed: at renewal credits count as pre-paid units for negotiating net-new discounts.

Scenario 3 (one-off credit block) — operational details:
- Billing: single PO for the block, invoice upon signature.
- Credits: expirations set to 6 months; larger blocks receive volume discount (5–12% stepped).

Docs & timeline:
- I’ve created the amendment draft (attached by Ben) and the DocuSign checklist.
- For Oct 12 PO approval target, we need signed amendment + PO by Oct 9 to get legal routing completed.

Next steps from our side:
1) Ben: pick the scenario you want to recommend to the customer based on risk appetite.
2) NovaWorks: confirm preferred conversion (credits vs refund) and procurement timeline.
3) Redwood Legal/RevOps: finalize amendment & DocuSign envelope.

Lauren Bishop
Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
